title: CPU shortages hit cloud infrastructure as AI agent workloads drive demand surge
content:
A CPU shortage is now hitting cloud infrastructure, following prior GPU and memory shortages, driven largely by AI agent workloads that consume heavy CPU resources for tool usage, code compilation, testing, and reinforcement learning. Spot pricing has largely disappeared, reservations now require months of lead time, and even large companies are being turned down by cloud providers due to capacity limits. Contributing factors include TSMC prioritizing GPU production over CPUs, DRAM manufacturers shifting to high-bandwidth memory over regular DRAM, and AI data centers shifting CPU-to-GPU ratios from 1:8 toward 1:1. Server order fulfillment has stretched from 1-2 weeks to about six months, with prices up 10-20%. Companies are advised to start capacity planning up to 12 months ahead, review CPU efficiency of existing services, and consider locking in fixed capacity even at higher cost given growing demand.
Questions this post answers
Why is there a CPU shortage in cloud computing right now?
AI agent workloads and reinforcement learning training are consuming far more CPU capacity than before, since agents run tools like compilers, test suites, and linters on CPUs while RL training requires CPUs to run and evaluate software. Manufacturing capacity is also squeezed: TSMC prioritizes GPU production over CPUs, and DRAM makers favor high-bandwidth memory over regular DRAM needed by CPUs. Teams sizing cloud infrastructure for agentic workloads can follow ongoing coverage of compute shortages on daily.dev.
How has cloud CPU spot pricing changed due to AI demand?
Spot pricing discounts of up to 90% off standard CPU prices have largely disappeared because there is no longer excess unused CPU capacity for providers to discount. Getting CPUs on spot instances is now nearly impossible without long-running contracts with cloud providers, and dedicated reservations must be made months in advance. Engineers planning cloud spend around spot instances can track pricing shifts like this on daily.dev.
How far in advance should companies plan CPU capacity reservations with cloud providers now?
Companies should plan CPU capacity up to 12 months in advance, since server orders that used to be fulfilled in 1-2 weeks now take roughly six months, with prices up 10-20%. Some cloud regions no longer accept new tenants because all CPU capacity is already leased, and some customers are prepaying for capacity that will only come online months later. Infrastructure teams building out capacity forecasts can follow shortage trends like this on daily.dev.

report.summary: AI智能体需求激增，云CPU出现短缺
report.background: 继GPU和内存短缺之后，CPU正成为云基础设施的新瓶颈。AI智能体在工具调用、代码编译、测试和强化学习评估中大量消耗CPU，同时供给端受挤压：台积电优先生产GPU，DRAM厂商转向高带宽内存HBM，AI数据中心CPU与GPU配比从1:8走向1:1。结果是Spot折扣消失、预留需提前数月、服务器交付从1-2周拉长到约6个月，价格上涨10-20%。企业被建议提前12个月做容量规划并锁定长期资源。
key_points: AI智能体把CPU变成新瓶颈：工具调用、编译、测试和强化学习都重耗CPU，传统云负载难以匹敌。
供给端双重挤压：台积电优先GPU产能，DRAM厂转产HBM，导致服务器CPU和普通内存供给受限。
云采购明显变难：Spot折扣基本消失，预留需提前数月，部分云区域已停止接纳新租户。
交付与价格恶化：服务器订单从1-2周拉长到约6个月，价格普遍上涨10-20%。
企业应对策略：提前12个月规划容量，审查现有服务CPU效率，并考虑高价锁定固定容量。
report.impact: 对AI行业，算力瓶颈从GPU扩散到CPU，智能体规模化部署成本上升，可能推动专用CPU、异构计算和效率优化。对开发者，云成本上涨、Spot难抢，需优化代码与容器密度，并尽早预留容量。对普通用户，AI服务可能涨价、限流或功能上线变慢，最终间接承担成本。
report.tools: 可关注云厂商容量与成本工具：AWS Cost Explorer、Azure Advisor、GCP Recommender；K8s弹性调度用Karpenter、KEDA；能效与成本监控用Kepler、OpenCost；编译加速用Bazel、ccache，以降低CPU压力。
